title: Why Your Tongue Sticks to a Frozen Pole
description:
Why does your tongue stick to a frozen pole? Your own spit turns into glue. Metal pulls heat out of your wet tongue far faster than wood or plastic, so the saliva freezes in a flash, right into the tiny bumps of your tongue and the tiny pits in the metal. The ice locks them together.

If it ever happens: never pull, because the ice can tear the skin. Pour warm (not hot) water on the spot, the ice melts, and your tongue comes free.

Have you ever seen someone get stuck? Tell us below.

More true whys: https://www.youtube.com/@truewhys?sub_confirmation=1

Sources: Live Science, "Will Your Tongue Really Stick to a Frozen Flagpole?"; How It Works, "Why does a warm tongue stick to a frozen object?"; Gizmodo; Today I Found Out.
